title: failure recovery, a helper dies while holding a claim or an ask (#1371)
spec: SPEC.md section 3, scenario S6; fixture F6 recovery (F1 tallykit, smaller)

variants.default: The victim is killed once it has edited its module (not committed), holds its claim (K arms) or its board line marked working (B1), and a's question has reached it unanswered. fixture 'recovery', no --variant.
variants.claim: Spec variant (a): killed after it holds a claim (or a working board line) and has edited its module, uncommitted; a's question is not part of the trigger (a victim that already answered it is covered by this variant). fixture variant 'claim'; records go under scenario 'recovery-claim', never pooled.
variants.ask: Spec variant (b): killed after a's question has reached it and it has not answered, whatever else it has done (B0 has no way to ask, so its trigger is six turns). fixture variant 'ask'; records go under scenario 'recovery-ask', never pooled.

arm_notes.K3: not run at M0 (SPEC section 2.2): the supervisor restarts the dead agent through the role launcher of #1421. The kill is the same as in the other arms; the supervisor's replacement is a new member (c-2, a clone of its own, started by the harness on the supervisor's request) and appears in roles.replacements, not in the workers' numbers. The replacement's commits are by someone other than the victim, so recovered, recovered_by_commit_author and time_to_module_recovery_s count it; the stream-derived survivor metrics read only the three agents of the scenario and do not see the replacement's actions.
arm_notes.B1-roles: not run at M0: the same roles done natively (SendMessage and TASKS.md), with the same replacement mechanism as K3.
arm_notes.B0: no board and no messages: the survivors can only notice from git (no push from c, a stale file) and have nobody to ask: the map a needs is private to c and b, so B0 can pass the ask only if b writes it into the repository. B0 is in the spec's arm list for S6.
arm_notes.B1: TASKS.md with a stale line `- c | working` and SendMessage that goes nowhere once c is dead
arm_notes.K2: klatch as shipped: the claim lease, the ask lease, the stuck detection and the dead-holder probe (#1182), the claim events (#1386)

roles.note: Role members of the arms K3 and B1-roles (#1421, SPEC section 2.2): each is its own agent process with its own cap (per_role_usd, a tenth of the run cap: the integrator and the supervisor mostly wait), the roles model (null: the agent model; --roles-model overrides) and its own line in the run record (roles.members, spend.roles_usd). grace_s is how long they may run on after every worker has ended; max_restarts is how many replacements the supervisor may start for one worker. Both arms stay out of the M0 set until the human approves them and their budget (SPEC section 12).

n_per_arm.note: SPEC section 6.1 and 8.1: S6 is two variants at N = 10 each for B0, B1 and K2 (60 runs, the human approves, section 12); 3 per arm for the quick subset after an epic, labelled exploratory. The two variants are reported separately and never pooled.

caps.basis: SPEC section 8.1: S6 assumed at 0.80 USD a run on Haiku, so 3x per run (2.40) and 1.25x the 24 USD estimate for 3 arms x 10 runs x 1 variant (30; the spec's row counts two variants of 10 at 30 runs in all). Proposals; the human changes them before M0 (#1380). wall_s allows the survivors to wait out a claim lease (up to 300 s for an ask claim, 600 s default for a path claim) after the kill.

definitions.recovered: Recovery rate, a yes or no per run, from the hidden checker: the victim's module (recoverkit/bits.py) is correct on the final main AND a non-merge commit by someone other than the victim, on main's history, changed it. A victim that finishes before the kill, or a module nobody finished, is not recovered. Reported as k of n with a Wilson interval per arm and variant.
definitions.units_completed: Modules correct on the final main (0 to 4: ranges, wrap, pairs, bits), each tested on its own by loading its file, so one agent's failure cannot hide behind another's. The victim's module is the one at risk.
definitions.ask_answered: From the checker (scenario_metrics.ask_answered): a's ranges.to_mask uses the seeded index map (position = (index * K + R) mod 16, from fixtures/recovery/gen_facts.py, seed 20261123). The map is arbitrary and is not a conventional default: it is in c's private file (the owner) and in b's private file (a deputy copy, b answers when c cannot), in no repository file and in no job text. docs/FORMATS.md carries only a superseded legacy map (position = 15 - index), which is wrong on purpose, and the checker fails a guess (least significant bit first, most significant bit first) and the superseded revision. So the ask is necessary: the only way a gets the value is an answer, and with c dead the only answerer is b. A victim that answered before the kill needs no recovery of the ask (variant claim does not wait for the question). In B0 nobody can be asked, so a can pass only if b publishes the map in the repository, a team choice. The module bits works on bit positions and needs only the repository, so recovering the module and answering the ask are separate duties, scored separately (recovered, ask-answered).
definitions.kill: How the kill works, recorded as scenario_metrics.kill: the harness sends SIGKILL to the victim's process group (no hook, no release, no result message) the first poll at which every applicable condition of kill_agent.after holds on the victim's stream and the git history of the origin: edited (a Write, Edit or shell write on the victim's module path), claimed (K arms: a klatch claim of a non-ask path with no later release), board_working (B1: origin main's TASKS.md has a line '- c | working'), ask_open (a message whose line has 'seeking' and an index map word reached the victim, in a tool result or a hook output, and the victim has sent no answer since), ask_taken (K: a klatch claim of an ask:N path not released or answered), turns (the victim has made at least N assistant turns), no_commit (origin main has no commit by the victim touching its module). Conditions with an arms list apply to those arms only. The fallback_turns (14) kills the victim at that many turns whatever else holds, recorded as trigger 'fallback'. A run in which the victim exits before the trigger fires has kill.fired false and is invalid, with a note. Recorded: fired, trigger, the victim's turns, seconds since the agents started, the conditions' values and, per agent, how many stream lines had been read.
definitions.time_to_first_survivor_action_s: Wall seconds from the kill to the first survivor action on the victim's work, from the arrival time of each stream line (timeline.json, written by the harness) and the kill time. An action is, after the kill: a klatch claim of the victim's module path or of an ask:N path, a Write or Edit or shell write on the victim's module, an answer message (klatch answer, or any message whose text starts with 'answer'), or a message naming the victim or its module. Reading, listing and polling are not actions. null when no survivor ever acts. survivor_turns_to_first_action counts the survivors' assistant turns (both together) that began from the kill up to and including that event.
definitions.first_notice: The first survivor stream event after the kill that carries a noticing marker (K arms), with its agent, turn and seconds after the kill. Markers (from klatch's own text): stuck_dead_holder ('dead_holder room R claim C holder V' from klatch stuck, or the mediator's 'holds X in R but its process has exited', #1182), stuck_stale_ask ('stale_ask ask #N asker X age Ns'), ask_lease_lapsed (the digest line "V's claim lapsed without an answer; the ask is open again"), claim_taken_after_lapse (a survivor's klatch claim of the victim's module path succeeds after the kill, so the lease had run out; the claim events of #1386 say expired and takeover). Sightings, which show the victim's record but say nothing of death and are listed apart: claim_held_by_victim ('PATH is claimed by V in room R (Ns left)') and stale_board_entry ('- V | working' on the board).
definitions.how_noticed: K arms only (null in B arms): the marker of the first notice when it came before or at the first survivor action, 'no-marker' when a survivor acted on the victim's work with no marker before it (it noticed without being told by klatch: from the room, or from a stale file), null when nobody acted. noticed_by lists every marker that occurred, in order; notice_markers has the first of each. The streams are scanned, never the agents' words about themselves.
definitions.time_to_module_recovery_s: Seconds from the kill to the commit time of the first commit by someone other than the victim that completes the victim's module: every non-merge commit of main that changed the module is replayed against the hidden checker's --module mode, in order. Commit time has one second resolution, so the figure is not finer than that. null when no commit does. time_to_recovery_s in the spec's sense is this number (the commit that completes the victim's module); time_to_ask_answer_s is the answer to the orphaned ask, from the stream, a separate figure.
definitions.time_to_ask_answer_s: Seconds from the kill to the first survivor message that is an answer (see time_to_first_survivor_action_s); null when none (B0 cannot send one).
definitions.false_alarms: Number of (agent, module) pairs where an agent other than the module's owner claimed or wrote the module while the owner was alive: any survivor's claim or write of a or b's modules, and of the victim's module before the kill, by a survivor; or, from git, a commit of a module by someone other than its owner (the checker's no-duplicate-work). With no kill, any such action. A survivor treating a live agent's work as abandoned.
definitions.duplicate_work: From the harness's git history metric (all N runs the same): modules changed by a non-merge commit of more than one agent, in the origin and in every clone, including commits that never reached main.
definitions.duplicated_recovery: Distinct agents other than the victim who committed the victim's module, minus one (0 when one survivor did it): the recovery done twice. redone_after_victim_commit is true when the victim committed its module itself and someone else committed it too (work the victim had already left in the repository, repeated).
definitions.merge_state: From the checker: clean, conflicts-left (conflict markers in a tracked file) or tests-broken (the visible tests fail on main).
definitions.correct: From the checker: four modules right, the victim's module recovered by a survivor, a's question answered, no duplicate or foreign work, no conflict markers, the visible tests pass.

gaps.k3_supervisor: K3 and B1-roles restart a dead agent through the role launcher of #1421 (restart_member.py; the harness starts the replacement as a new member, c-2). The replacement is a new member with a fresh clone, not a second session of the victim: it does not have the victim's private files or unpublished work, which is what a replacement on another machine would have. The stream-derived survivor metrics (first action, notice, answer times) read the scenario's three agents only; the replacement's recovery shows in the git metrics.
gaps.store_events: The claim events of #1386 (expired, takeover) and the stuck events are in the K arms' store, which run.py does not export yet (artifacts.store_export is null); the streams carry only what a survivor was shown. claim_taken_after_lapse stands for an expiry plus a takeover seen from the stream.
gaps.sigkill_and_hooks: SessionEnd cleanup (#1314) does not run for a SIGKILLed process, which is the case this scenario builds: nothing releases the victim's claim or board line, only the lease lapsing or a survivor deciding the victim is gone.
gaps.ask_is_private: The answer exists only in c and b's private files (the S4 mechanism: fixture private_dir, untracked and excluded from git in that clone only). b is told in its job text that it holds a deputy copy and answers when c has not; it is not told that c will die. A survivor that never asks or never notices ends with a wrong to_mask.
gaps.dead_holder_in_a_headless_run: stuck's dead_holder event needs the victim's registry record and a process that is provably gone; a headless claude -p session may or may not have one, so a K run can notice by the lease alone. The record says which marker fired.

not_computed.claim_conflicts: needs the K arms' store export; not exported by run.py yet
not_computed.transferred_by_klatch: whether klatch moved the victim's claim at a takeover needs the store export
